_comment: MODELLED projection, not measured data. The car is not metered separately from the house, so annual mileage, efficiency and charging losses are estimates. The baseline is the two cars actually replaced, at real-world economy rather than manufacturer figures, and at UK average pump prices as of September 2026. Replace with measured figures once a full year of charging is logged and mark measured:true.

tracker._comment: Running cost tracker, built by scripts/aggregate.mjs from the `car` blocks in data/daily/*.json (MySkoda odometer + SoC; charging kWh estimated from the car's reported charging state/power, split home off-peak / home peak / away). Each day's EV cost = home kWh at the import tariff in force + away kWh at away_p_per_kwh + the net battery drop over the window (SoC) priced at the off-peak rate grossed up for charging losses. Each day's fuel cost = miles driven x the two old cars' blended pence-per-mile at that week's UK pump prices (DESNZ weekly road fuel prices). Starts at the first full day of MySkoda data.
tracker.away_note: Public charging on trips (France and the Netherlands, Oct 2026), about 50p/kWh as reported by the owner. Home charging is nearly all on the IOG overnight rate.

replaced.note: Two cars, roughly half the mileage each. The Enyaq is now the only car.

fuel_sensitivity._note: annual cost GBP for 10,000 miles if pump prices rise from the Sept 2026 baseline of 167p petrol / 189p diesel
